notes.heading: Ideal gas model assumptions
points: Ideal gas particles move constantly and strike the container walls; these impacts create the gas pressure.
Particle volume is negligible compared with the volume of the container.
There are no intermolecular forces between particles.
All collisions between particles are elastic, so no kinetic energy is lost.
Kinetic energy of the particles is directly proportional to the Kelvin temperature.

notes.heading: Real gases deviate from ideal behaviour
points: Real gases deviate when intermolecular forces are detectable and/or the molecules fill a significant part of the container volume.
Deviation is greatest at low temperature and high pressure; ideal behaviour is best at high temperature and low pressure.
Low temperature: slower molecules let attractions form, so collisions may not be elastic.
High pressure: molecule volume becomes significant, so doubling pressure no longer halves the volume.
Forces between molecules reduce collisions with the walls, lowering the measured pressure of a real gas.

notes.heading: Molar volume and gas relationships
points: Equal volumes of any gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of particles (Avogadro).
Molar volume of an ideal gas is constant at a given temperature and pressure; at STP it is 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹.
STP: 273.15 K (0 °C) and 100.0 kPa. Molar mass M = m/n, where n = V/Vm.
At constant T and n, p is inversely proportional to V: pV = constant; p against 1/V is a straight line.
At constant V, p is proportional to Kelvin T; at constant p, V is proportional to Kelvin T.

notes.heading: Ideal gas equation and combined law
points: Combined gas law: p1V1/T1 = p2V2/T2 for a fixed amount of gas. Temperature must be in kelvin (K = °C + 273.15).
Ideal gas equation: pV = nRT, with p in Pa, V in m³, T in K, n in mol.
R is about 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ with SI units; kPa with dm³ gives the same R.
Molar mass of a gas: find n = pV/RT, then M = m/n.
Keep units consistent in the combined gas law: both pressures in the same unit, both volumes in the same unit.

definitions.definition: A gas whose particles have negligible volume, no intermolecular forces, and collide elastically while moving constantly.
definitions.trap: Saying ideal gas particles have zero movement; they are in constant motion.

definitions.definition: A gas that deviates from the ideal gas model because of intermolecular forces and/or the significant volume of its molecules.
definitions.trap: Forgetting that deviation is greatest at low temperature and high pressure.

definitions.definition: Reference conditions for gases of 273.15 K (0 °C) and 100.0 kPa pressure.
definitions.trap: Using 101.3 kPa or 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ instead of 100.0 kPa and 22.7.

definitions.term: Molar volume of an ideal gas
definitions.definition: The volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas, constant at a specified temperature and pressure; 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹ at STP.
definitions.trap: Quoting molar volume without stating that it applies only at the given temperature and pressure.

definitions.definition: Equal volumes of any two gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles.
definitions.trap: Leaving out the same temperature and pressure condition.

definitions.definition: The universal constant in pV = nRT, approximately 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ when p, V, T and n are in SI units.
definitions.trap: Using non-SI units for p or V while still using 8.31.
